faq: How much data do I need for segments?
A few hundred contacts and some order history is enough to start. With a smaller list, we build fewer, broader groups, because tiny segments give you too little to send to.
Will segments update on their own?
Yes. We build dynamic segments, so people move in and out as they buy or go quiet. We test the rules with sample customers, so you can see them behave correctly.
Do you use personal data in a way that is safe?
We use only data you already collected through your store and forms, and respect consent. We never build segments based on sensitive traits, and we do not move data outside your own tools.
Which tools can you build segments in?
Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Omnisend, Brevo and similar tools. Segments are easiest in Klaviyo, and we tell you if your plan limits what can be done.

desc:
Email and SMS customer segmentation sorts your contacts into groups so each message fits the person reading it. Ecom Swift LLC builds the segments inside your own tool from real order and activity data, then explains what each group is for and what to send it.

## What is customer segmentation?

Customer segmentation is the practice of dividing your contacts into groups based on shared traits or behavior, such as what they bought, how recently, how much they spent or what they clicked. A segment is a live rule, not a fixed list: people join and leave it automatically as their activity changes.

Email and SMS tools can build segments from signup data, order history and engagement. The work is deciding which groups are worth having and defining them correctly.

## Why one message for everyone falls short

A first-time buyer, a loyal customer and someone who has not opened an email in a year need different things. Sending all three the same newsletter means the message is wrong for at least two of them. Irrelevant messages teach people to ignore you or to unsubscribe.

Segments solve this by letting you say the right thing to the right group. New subscribers can be welcomed, first-time buyers can be guided toward a second purchase, loyal customers can get early access, and inactive contacts can be asked whether they still want to hear from you. Sending less to the wrong people also helps protect your sender reputation. Outcomes depend on your catalog and data, but relevance is a reliable reason people stay subscribed.

## What a useful segment set includes

- New subscribers who have not yet bought.
- First-time buyers, kept apart from repeat buyers.
- Repeat buyers and loyal customers.
- High-value and low-value customers, defined by your own spend levels.
- Shoppers interested in one collection or product type.
- Highly engaged contacts who click regularly.
- Inactive contacts who have stopped opening or clicking.
- Suppression of unsubscribed and bounced addresses, so they never receive sends.
- Back-in-stock and wishlist groups, where your tool tracks them.
- A one-page guide naming each segment and suggesting what to send it.

## How we build the groups

We begin by looking at the data your tool already holds: orders, products, signup source and email or text activity. Then we agree which groups suit your business, define each one precisely and check the counts against what you expect. A segment that includes everyone, or no one, is usually wrongly defined.

Basic builds five core segments around buying behavior, with suppression and a one-page guide. Standard builds ten, including collection and value segments, gives a send suggestion for each and runs an internal test send. Premium builds eighteen, adding engagement scoring, back-in-stock and wishlist groups and a sunset plan for contacts who stopped responding, with a handover call. Add-ons include extra segments, a customer value report and a segmented campaign. We use only data you already have, in the way your consent records allow.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with a few groups you will really use.
- Name each segment so anyone can understand it.
- Check counts after any change in your store data.
- Give inactive contacts one clear chance to stay before removal.
- Respect channel consent: email consent is not text consent.

**Avoid:**
- Building dozens of overlapping groups no one sends to.
- Using sensitive personal details to target messages.
- Texting a segment that never agreed to texts.
- Treating an old segment as correct without a check.
- Sending the same offer to every group with only the name changed.

## Who it is for

A store with a growing list that mixes new and loyal customers will see the clearest use. A brand with several product lines can send each group news about its own collection. A seller worried about falling engagement can identify and manage inactive contacts carefully.

## What we need from you

Tell us your email or SMS tool, share a short description of your products and customers and mention any groups you already have in mind. We never need your password. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the tool supports it, and you stay the owner of the account and data.
